messages.author: 1c993cc05f18470a
messages.subject: WLSMV estimator and missing="pairwise"
parts:
Dear all,

Does anybody of you know, if I can use an "WLSMV" estimator and missing  "pairwise"?

I'm trying to fit a RI-CLPM in lavaan with 4 categorical timepoints , and so I guess by default with the ordered argument the estimater should be "WLSMV" ... I have binary, incomplete data which is non-normal distributed.

fit <- sem(riclpmMACanViolmodel, data = Data, ordered =c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "y1", "y2", "y3", "y4"), missing="pairwise")

summary(fit,  fit.measures = T, standardized = T)

Thank you very much for your help.

Michelle

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator and missing="pairwise"
parts:
Hi
This is a default option in lavaan for missing data. I think no problem arise if missingness in your data is low and random. Otherwise you should take another strategy for your missing. Bellow link from mplus site has some recomendation for missing dats. Lavaan and mplus hava large common options

http://www.statmodel.com/discussion/messages/9/9587.html?1423546955

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator and missing="pairwise"
parts: This is a default option in lavaan for missing data.

No, the default is listwise, but pairwise is the only other option for DWLS estimation.  Also for estimator="PML", which is also an option for ordinal indicators.

https://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/pml/PL_Tutorial.pdf
